I agree that the game's concept is solid, but since it's still in Early Access, it clearly needs further development. I also feel the current price is excessive; in my opinion, it should be closer to $5 or $6. Despite these issues, I thoroughly enjoyed the one round I played as a zombie. It's essentially like Dead by Daylight, but with a great twist: instead of repairing generators, you are focused on defending your position. I believe the fundamental idea behind the game is quite strong, and it definitely has the potential to be developed into something truly great

Full disclosure, I've been part of the closed beta for the last few months and I love the game. There's definitely a learning curve especially if you're coming from 7dd or if you're playing as ZM but if you play for more than an hour or two you'll get the hang of it. You certainly won't have a good time if all you do is dig through the game files for 45 minutes to satisfy your nerd rage or if you've pigeonholed yourself into a 7dd youtube channel and can't find another game to monetise. I give the game 5 thumbs up and 12/5 stars.

The game it's unplayable atm, took me 2 hours to find 3 matches and one of the matches crashed before it ended. Not only it takes forever for the game to find players to join your match, after the game finds your team, at the ready up stage if someone leaves, the matchmaking lobby breaks, forcing everyone to leave and go back to the 10+ minute queue to find players. Sometimes it takes a long time to find servers too. When the game crashes there's no way to go back to your previous match, they just send you back to the queues, ending up waiting another 30 minutes or more for a game. If it wasn't for all of that I think the game could have been a fun gamek, the concept it's fine, but there's no rewards because they are all overpriced receolor skins from 7d2d that they are expecting you to end up paying real money for, because there's no way you can grind the currency they are asking for them. P.s.: In 2 hours of gameplay I got 60 flasks. The cheapest transmog in the game costs 50.000 flasks. (Or €3,29) Not going to tell you they are forcing us to buy the items with real money! Very Good Game. Now with that being said it is in EARLY ACCESS. So there are some bugs and kinks in the game that are still being worked out. Only so much can be done inside Beta Testing and when going from that to live run some of the previous bugs can reappear but it seems they are trying to work on those. Kinda gives the vibe of 7 days to die, meets Left for Dead, with a bit of Dead by Daylight sprinkled in. The game is pretty straightforward at the moment of gather resources through the day survive by night. Becareful though, the Zombie Master can target and destroy your resources. The game can get a bit repetitive and grindy. There are only so many levels to play on right now but at least each level has a differently variants scaling in how much destruction of the area has already taken place before the match starts. (ie: buildings destroyed, standing, or in states of decay.) I do believe there is room to improve in the upgrade system for ZM (Zombie Master) and the survivors, Along with the levels. All said and done have to remember it is an Early access game. With that taken into consideration, to gameplay, mechanics, and all presentation i would say a solid 3.5 out of 5. Deffinantly needs some tweaks in both game play and some of the mechanics behind it.

Absolute garbage balancing; you cannot win against a zombie player with half a brain cell unless you have a full team of 4 which is impossible to do when nobody plays the game. Progression is oppressively slow for the only thing to change is the numbers on your gun -> there is also no individual gun customization for attachments. The maps are small, I've already played all of them and they all generally play the same. Building anything of value is impossible as the system is practically unusable while also only having 1:30-2 minutes before the next wave comes once you've finished looting. (the zombie player can put everything they have into speed and just strafe back and forth hitting you at Mach 3 which just makes me alt-f4)

Game is dead. Mostly its only about 40players online, with a quarter of it being the devs. Leveling and upgrading up got to be frustrating as well. You need to win between 20 and 40 games for an upgrade for survivors. Leveling up Zombie Master is even more of a grind. Whats part of the problem, that only a few players are willing to play as a zombie master. Depending on the time youre playing its impossible to get a full game lobby, despite searching world wide. And what pisses me of the most: This game was almost 20€ on release. Two weeks later they reduced the price down to below 10€. I really really wanted this game to be good. And spent a few evenings playing it with friends. But only with them, because you're not able to get a full lobby with randoms. Because there is no playerbase left for this...

This game is great, i think its a good side project for the developers of 7 days to die but for it to do better i think it just needs a few changes. The zombies are extremely fast and it makes the intentionally arcade like game a little too arcady, additionally each round doesnt last super long for balancing reasons, but i think its fine if we dont change this. But one very large issue is how weak builds are and how zombies can spawn on top of your builds, you can build a huge wall with tons of spikes for it to be broken down in a few swings, besides they can even just spawn on you, plus they dont even give many resources or ammo at all so you have to go primarily melee on hordes which to me defeats the purpose of many features because they are so weak. other wise the game is still fun and worth playing.
